bluf: GAME DAY + SATURDAY NIGHT — Texas vs Florida at Darrell K. Royal Stadium (11:00 AM per City of Austin listing; ~100,000 seats; 1.5 mi N on San Jacinto Blvd, the hotel's own street) drives heavy pedestrian, rideshare and I-35 traffic; Austin FC vs Vancouver follows at Q2 Stadium (7:30 PM). Weather is benign: breezy and cool, high 69-72F, N gusts 25-35 mph through the morning, no advisories. Crime pattern to brief: Oct 13 note-passing bank robbery at the 100 block of Congress Ave (suspect arrested within 2 minutes; no device), Oct 16 shooting inside a moving vehicle at W 10th and N Lamar (possible suspect in custody; occupants knew each other), and the Sep 13 armed robbery of off-duty soldiers at E 6th and Sabine at bar close (3 arrested). Civil unrest is low: nonpartisan No Kings Vote Early events are voter-outreach focused with the Austin events in the suburbs and north Austin, but anti-ICE protests continue as a backdrop. US-Iran: no agreement in force; reporting is contradictory; no direct Austin nexus.

incidents.title: TEXAS VS FLORIDA GAME DAY - DARRELL K. ROYAL STADIUM
incidents.location: DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, 2139 San Jacinto Blvd (~1.5 mi N)
incidents.relevance: San Jacinto Blvd is the hotel's frontage street, so guest arrivals, valet queues and rideshare pickup will be congested. Opposing-fan visitors are likely among guests. Post-game crowds will push into the Red River, 6th Street and Rainey districts and the bars/restaurant. Confirm the kickoff time before shift briefing; listings vary.
incidents.detail: Texas Longhorns host Florida Gators; City of Austin lists an 11:00 AM start. Stadium capacity is roughly 100,000. A Waterloo Park tailgate runs 8 AM-noon (500 E 12th St, ~0.8 mi N). Expect heavy foot, rideshare and vehicle flow on San Jacinto Blvd, Red River, I-35 and the Cesar Chavez corridor from early morning, with egress and downtown bar traffic from mid-afternoon into the evening.

incidents.title: DOWNTOWN ROBBERY / SHOOTING PATTERN - RECENT 72 HOURS TO 5 WEEKS
incidents.location: 100 blk Congress Ave; W 10th & N Lamar; E 6th & Sabine
incidents.relevance: Congress Ave bank is roughly 0.2 mi from the property: expect elevated APD presence; no ongoing threat. The E 6th/Sabine armed-robbery pattern is directly relevant to guests walking to Saturday-night bars after game day; suspects are in custody but the tactic (bar-close, group targeting, getaway vehicle) persists. Advise concierge to steer late-night walkers to rideshare and to well-lit routes.
incidents.detail: (1) Oct 13: a man handed a Wells Fargo teller a note claiming he had a bomb at the 100 block of Congress Ave; APD arrested Makiya Johnson within about 2 minutes. No device reported. (2) Oct 16, ~7:18 PM: a driver was shot by someone inside his vehicle and crashed near W 10th St and N Lamar Blvd (~0.9 mi NW); he was in surgery; APD said all occupants knew each other and a possible suspect was in custody. (3) Sep 13, 2:25 AM at bar close: a juvenile robbed a woman near E 6th and Sabine, then he and a second juvenile (with a Draco rifle) robbed three off-duty Army service members, one shot in the face and survived; Alijah Rodriguez (18) and two juveniles were arrested Sep 22.

incidents.title: CAPITOL THREAT ARREST (SEP 30) - NO ONGOING THREAT PER DPS
incidents.relevance: Informational: demonstrates the lone-actor threat pattern near downtown government sites. No change to posture. Capitol grounds close at 8 PM daily; DPS monitors demonstrations there.
incidents.detail: Texas DPS and the FBI arrested Benny Caldera Jr., 40, of Converse on Sep 30 after credible information of a planned violent attack on the Capitol on Oct 1. He was charged with felony terroristic threat against a public servant, then taken into federal custody on additional federal charges. An official briefed on the case told ABC News he had been threatening a mass shooting and had been collecting ammunition and guns. DPS stated there is no reason to believe there is an ongoing threat to the Capitol, legislators, staff or the public.

incidents.title: US-IRAN WAR / TALKS - NO AGREEMENT IN FORCE
incidents.relevance: No direct Austin nexus. Possible effects: fuel and energy cost swings, travel disruption for international guests, and protest activity at federal sites if strikes resume. Monitor for a sudden escalation that could change the heightened-awareness posture.
incidents.detail: The June 17 Islamabad memorandum collapsed over shipping in early July and one tracker reports it expired unextended Aug 17. Reporting on current status is contradictory: Iranian and Reuters-sourced reports describe intensified efforts toward a preliminary deal and a frozen-funds mechanism, while others report US-Iran air strikes and Iran calling the ceasefire meaningless. Mediators (Qatar, Pakistan, Egypt) continue to pass messages. One analysis says Washington has pledged no strikes before the Nov 3 midterms. Treat the situation as unresolved and volatile.

civil_unrest.title: No Kings: Vote Early - Austin Events
civil_unrest.location: Circle C (9-10 AM), Onion Creek (10 AM-noon), First UU Church, 4700 Grover Ave (2-5 PM)
civil_unrest.detail: Nationwide 'No Kings: Vote Early' day (2,500+ events) is billed as nonpartisan voter participation, not purely a protest; organizers prohibit weapons and civil disobedience. Austin listings are outer-area or north-central (4700 Grover Ave is ~4 mi N). None are listed downtown today, unlike the March 28 No Kings march from City Hall to Auditorium Shores that drew thousands. Spontaneous downtown turnout is possible given the wider political climate.

civil_unrest.title: Anti-ICE Protest Backdrop (Garces Perez Shooting)
civil_unrest.location: Texas Capitol; Anderson Sq / Research Blvd (N Austin)
civil_unrest.detail: Protests have continued since the Sep 20 shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez by an ICE officer in North Austin. Capitol-area crowds were ~150-200 and dispersed peacefully; the N Austin site saw 4 arrests on riot-related charges on Sep 20 and a City Council candidate was arrested Sep 26 on a riot-participation warrant. A federal judge temporarily halted his deportation. No specific downtown action is announced for today, but flash demonstrations at the Capitol remain possible (grounds close at 8 PM).

Sources disagree on whether recent strikes occurred and whether a preliminary deal is close; treat as unresolved. Possible energy-cost and travel effects only.

Lone-actor threats: the Sep 30 arrest of a man accused of planning a mass shooting at the Texas Capitol shows the threat pattern near downtown government sites. DPS reports no ongoing threat.
